pages.title: Master the Main Git Commands
pages.subtitle: A comic cheat sheet for the commands you'll use most

panels.heading: What Git Does
panels.body:
Tracks changes in your code.
Lets you save versions with commits.
Makes branching and collaboration easier.
Working directory (your files) -> staging area (prepare changes) -> repository (.git, saved history).
Git = time machine for your code.

panels.heading: Start Here
panels.body:
git init — create a new repo in the current folder.
git clone <url> — copy an existing repo.
git remote -v — view connected remotes.
panels.code:
git init
git clone <url>
git remote -v

panels.heading: See Changes / Stage Files
panels.body:
git status — see changed, staged, and untracked files.
git add <file> — stage one file.
git add . — stage all current changes.
git restore --staged <file> — unstage a file.
File (changed) -> stage (staged) -> repo (commit).
panels.code:
git status
git add <file>
git add .
git restore --staged <file>

panels.heading: Commit
panels.body:
git commit -m "message" — save staged changes.
git commit --amend — update the last commit.
Tip: good commit messages = short and specific.
Diagram: commit A -> commit B -> new commit (--amend) replaces the last one.
panels.code:
git commit -m "message"
git commit --amend

panels.heading: Branches
panels.body:
git branch — list branches.
git switch -c feature/login — create and switch to a new branch.
git switch main — move to another branch.
git merge feature/login — merge a branch into the current branch.
Diagram: feature/login branches off main and merges back in.
panels.code:
git branch
git switch -c feature/login
git switch main
git merge feature/login

panels.heading: Push / Pull / Fetch
panels.body:
git push -u origin main — push and set upstream.
git push — send local commits to remote.
git pull — fetch + merge remote changes.
git fetch — download updates without merging.
Your machine pushes to the remote (server); pull and fetch bring changes back.
panels.code:
git push -u origin main
git push
git pull
git fetch

panels.heading: Look Around
panels.body:
git log --oneline --graph --all — compact history view.
git diff — inspect unstaged changes.
git diff --staged — inspect staged changes.
git show <commit> — inspect a specific commit.
Example output of git log --oneline --graph --all: a1b2c3d (HEAD -> main, origin/main) Fix login bug; e4f5a6b Add unit tests; c7d8e9f (feature/login) Add login page; 123abcd Initial commit.
panels.code:
git log --oneline --graph --all
git diff
git diff --staged
git show <commit>

panels.heading: Fix Mistakes
panels.body:
git restore <file> — discard local file changes.
git revert <commit> — make a new commit that undoes an old one.
git reset --soft HEAD~1 — undo last commit, keep changes staged.
git reset --hard HEAD~1 — erase last commit and local changes.
Use --hard carefully. It can't be undone.
panels.code:
git restore <file>
git revert <commit>
git reset --soft HEAD~1
git reset --hard HEAD~1

panels.heading: Useful Extras
panels.body:
git stash — save work temporarily.
git stash pop — restore stashed work.
git tag v1.0.0 — mark a release.
.gitignore — ignore files you don't want tracked.
Simple workflow: edit -> status -> add -> commit -> push.
panels.code:
git stash
git stash pop
git tag v1.0.0

pages.summary: A tour of everyday Git: how the working directory, staging area and repository relate, plus the core commands for starting a repo, staging, committing, branching, syncing with a remote, inspecting history and undoing mistakes.

pages.title: Git Cheat Sheet
pages.subtitle: The Essential Commands. Master Git. Ship confidently.

panels.heading: Setup & Config
panels.body: Set your name, set your email, check config, and set the default branch name for new repos.
panels.code:
# Set your name
git config --global user.name "Your Name"
# Set your email
git config --global user.email "you@example.com"
# Check config
git config --list
# Set default branch name (new repos)
git config --global init.defaultBranch main

panels.heading: Start a Repo
panels.body: Initialize a new repo, clone an existing repo, or show remote origins. Diagram: the remote (origin) syncs with your machine.
panels.code:
# Initialize new repo
git init
# Clone existing repo
git clone <repo-url>
# Show remote origins
git remote -v

panels.heading: Daily Workflow
panels.body: The flow: work -> add -> commit -> push. Repeat!
panels.code:
# See changes
git status
# Stage files
git add <file>    # or: git add .
# Commit changes
git commit -m "Your message"
# Push to remote
git push origin <branch>

panels.heading: Inspect & View
panels.body: Tip: use space to scroll in `less`, q to quit.
panels.code:
# See commit history (pretty)
git log --oneline --graph --decorate --all
# See changes in working directory
git diff
# See staged changes
git diff --staged
# Show info about a commit
git show <commit-hash>
# See file / branch details
git show <branch or file>

panels.heading: Branching
panels.body: Branches are lightweight and cheap. Diagram: a feature branch splits off main and runs alongside it.
panels.code:
# List branches
git branch
# Create new branch
git branch <new-branch>
# Switch branch
git checkout <branch>
# Create & switch
git checkout -b <new-branch>
# Delete branch
git branch -d <branch>
# Rename branch
git branch -m <new-name>

panels.heading: Undo & Recover
panels.body: Caution: git reset --hard can permanently lose work. Use with care!
panels.code:
# Unstage a file
git restore --staged <file>
# Discard changes in working dir
git restore <file>
# Revert a commit (safe)
git revert <commit-hash>
# Reset current branch (moves HEAD)
git reset --soft <commit>    # keep changes staged
git reset --mixed <commit>   # keep changes in working dir
git reset --hard <commit>    # discard all changes

panels.heading: Remotes
panels.body: Tip: FETCH = download; PULL = download + merge; PUSH = upload.
panels.code:
# Add remote
git remote add origin <repo-url>
# List remotes
git remote -v
# Fetch (download only)
git fetch origin
# Pull (fetch + merge)
git pull origin <branch>
# Push
git push origin <branch>
# Remove remote
git remote remove origin

panels.heading: Stash
panels.body: Perfect for context switching without committing!
panels.code:
# Stash current changes
git stash
# List stashes
git stash list
# Apply latest stash (keep in stash list)
git stash apply
# Apply & drop latest stash
git stash pop
# Apply specific stash
git stash apply stash@{2}
# Drop a stash
git stash drop stash@{2}

panels.heading: Cherry-Pick
panels.body:
Apply a specific commit from another branch. Diagram: commit C from feature/login (A-B-C) is copied as C' onto main (A-B), i.e. pick C onto main.
Great for small, isolated changes.
Conflict? Resolve, then run git cherry-pick --continue, or abort with git cherry-pick --abort.
panels.code:
# Apply a specific commit from another branch
git cherry-pick <commit-hash>
# After resolving a conflict
git cherry-pick --continue
# Or abort
git cherry-pick --abort

panels.heading: Merge vs Rebase — What's the Difference?
panels.body:
Merge (preserves history): keeps the full history; creates a merge commit (M); best for shared branches. Good for collaboration, when history matters.
Rebase (rewrites history): replays your commits on top (C1, C2 become C1', C2' after main's latest commit); keeps history clean & linear; best for local branches. Good for clean history before merging / PR.
When to use what? Use MERGE when: working on shared branches; you want to preserve full history; you want to show where branches met. Use REBASE when: cleaning up your own feature branch; preparing PR with a clean history; you haven't pushed (or coordinated) yet.
NEVER rebase commits that others have already based work on!
panels.code:
# Merge
git checkout main
git merge feature

# Rebase
git checkout feature
git rebase main

panels.heading: Tags & Releases
panels.code:
# List tags
git tag
# Create tag
git tag -a v1.0.0 -m "Version 1.0.0"
# Push tags
git push origin --tags
# Delete tag
git tag -d v1.0.0

panels.heading: Submodules (Basics)
panels.body: Use submodules for dependencies that live in their own repos.
panels.code:
# Add submodule
git submodule add <repo-url> path/
# Init & update
git submodule update --init --recursive
# Update submodule
git submodule update --remote --merge

panels.heading: Handy Aliases (Examples)
panels.body: Aliases = speed. Less typing, more shipping.
panels.code:
# Add these to ~/.gitconfig
[alias]
  st = status
  co = checkout
  br = branch
  ci = commit
  lg = log --oneline --graph --decorate --all

pages.footer: Good Git habits = fewer bugs, happier team, better you. Commit small & often. Write good messages. Pull before you push. Don't commit secrets.
pages.summary: A dense reference of essential Git commands grouped by task: setup, starting a repo, the daily add-commit-push loop, inspecting history, branching, undoing changes, remotes, stash, cherry-pick, tags, submodules and aliases. It also explains when to merge versus rebase.
